purpose: Tag-to-tag antenna delay calibration (step 1 of the fleet calibration plan: tags calibrated against each other first, then each anchor against a fixed-delay tag).
method: T1 (0x8052) stayed INIT/frame_index 0. T4 (0x7851) was temporarily set role=RESP, slot_index=7 (an unused slot, since A1-A7 occupy 0-6) and RESET to force the firmware's boot-time role dispatch to re-run -- SET,role + SAVE alone does not switch a live node's running state machine, only its NVS config; the state machine only re-dispatches on BOOT -> LOAD_CFG. Both boards were pinned to a common explicit baseline (ant_delay_tx=ant_delay_rx=16436, the vendor DW1000 example-code reference value) before measuring, rather than the CFG_ANT_DELAY_UNCAL sentinel (0xFFFF) T4 had defaulted to, so the correction is computed against a known symmetric starting point on both ends.
note: role, slot_index/frame_index, and ant_delay_tx/rx are NOT part of cfg_hash -- confirmed against core/cfg.c's cfg_hash_compute() field list before touching them -- so this entire procedure never desynced the rest of the fleet (hash stayed 0x02F3 throughout).

correction_math.source: Same constants core/ranging.c uses for ranging_ps_to_mm(), so this calibration's math matches the firmware's own.
correction_math.model: Spec eq(6): d = c*(tau - deltaA - deltaB). This firmware applies deltaA/deltaB by programming ant_delay_tx/ant_delay_rx directly into the DW1000's own antenna-delay registers (see core/ranging.h:78-79), not as a software subtraction -- so a distance deficit (measured < true) means too much delay is currently programmed and must be REDUCED, split evenly between the two identical-hardware tags, applied equally to each tag's own tx and rx register.

caveats: Single-baseline calibration, per the user's stated plan. A single distance can alias a directional/multipath bias into the delay estimate; recommended improvement (given, not yet applied) is 2-3 different distances/orientations averaged.

Per-sample SD stayed ~72-77mm across all three passes regardless of the mean converging -- that noise floor is inherent to this measurement (short range, indoor multipath), not something the antenna-delay correction can remove. The mean is reliable (SEM ~5.5mm) even though individual $RNG lines are noisy.

This is TAG-to-TAG calibration only (both boards identical ESP32 UWB Pro hardware, correction split evenly 50/50). Anchor calibration per the user's stated plan is a separate next step: a fixed-delay tag (e.g. this now-calibrated T1) against each anchor individually, anchor's own delay solved with the tag held fixed.
